question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To be at daggers drawn
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"To be at daggers drawn"** means to be in a state of extreme hostility or ready to fight. (लड़ने को तैयार होना)

 
 
• **Example: **After the heated argument, the two colleagues were at daggers drawn.
 
 
 
• **"Ready to fight"** means being prepared to engage in a confrontation or combat. (लड़ने के लिए तैयार)
 
 
• **Example: **The two nations were ready to fight after the diplomatic negotiations failed.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To be about to collapse **(ढहने वाला होना): Being on the verge of falling apart or failing.

 
 
• **Example:** The old building was about to collapse after the earthquake.
 
 
 
• **Under suspicion **(संदेह के तहत): Being suspected of wrongdoing.
 
 
• **Example: **The employee was under suspicion for embezzling company funds.
 
 
 
• **To be under control** (नियंत्रण में होना): Being managed or contained effectively.
 
 
• **Example:** The fire was finally under control after hours of effort by the firefighters.
 
 

3f:T934,

The correct answer is: **Option 4**.
